newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakia welcomes results of Amsterdam EU summit.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia welcomes results of Amsterdam EU summit.

text.p: Slovakia on Thursday welcomed the draft of a new agreement on the European Union, approved by an EU summit earlier this week in Amsterdam.

"In spite of the failure to solve all questions in the institutional sphere, the successful end of the Intergovernmental Conference (IGC) allows the process of enlargement of the union to be launched," the Slovak Foreign Ministry said in a statement, published in Slovak newspapers.
It said it appreciated the will of EU members to start as soon as possible concrete talks on acceptance of new members.
Slovakia, increasingly unlikely to be among the first wave of new NATO members, was warned on Wednesday it was also in danger of missing the train for integration into the EU.

European parliamentarians said after a meeting of a joint committee of the European and Slovak parliaments that a May referendum on NATO membership and presidential elections, which ended in chaos, had further weakened Slovakia's chances of being among leading contenders for EU enlargement.
In May, Slovakia appointed Foreign Minister Zdenka Kramplova to replace Pavol Hamzik who resigned over the domestic political situation and failed referendum.
"Membership in the European Union is the top priority of the government and also of the citizens of this country," the ministry said.
"The Slovak Republic will make maximum effort to fulfil the conditions for joining the EU," it added.
